reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports all key premises: it reports that Hf addition leads to Hf-rich phase precipitation at interfaces, that this hinders grain-boundary sliding and dislocation movement, that high-temperature strength and ductility improve (with an optimum around 0.5 at.%), and that room-temperature performance remains almost unchanged. Density preservation is implied by the unchanged phase morphology and is a standard expectation for trace additions, though not explicitly measured in the cited text.
premises: Hf addition (≈0.5 at.%) to Al17Cr10Fe36Ni36Mo1 promotes fine Hf-rich interfacial precipitates
Hf-rich precipitates hinder grain-boundary sliding and dislocation motion at high temperature
This precipitation strengthening improves high-temperature yield strength and ductility
Alloy density is not significantly increased
